Cc: vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com, ethan.park@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Access controls & support access — post-call recap

Thanks Jordan — great conversation this morning. Quick recap from the call and proposed next steps so we can keep the procurement and technical review moving.

Key items we covered:
- Data scope: PII elements you flagged (customer name, account_id, payment tokens) and how they flow through inference requests.
- Retention & logging: default audit/log retention, ability to extend for legal/FR requirements, and options for anonymization.
- Access controls: RBAC model, least-privilege roles, SCIM/SAML SSO integration and provisioning.
- Support access: just-in-time time-limited access, break-glass emergency flow with approvals & full audit trail.
- Data residency: US and EU region availability (you indicated US-only as preferred).

Actions / next steps (owners):
1) Technical deep-dive (Marissa & Vivek) — demo RBAC, support access flow, and audit logs. Proposed: Wed 2027-03-17 10:00 AM PT. (Marissa)
2) I will send our access-controls overview, SOC2 summary, and support-access playbook as attachments. (Marissa)
3) You to confirm the list of people who need read vs admin access and any residency/legal constraints. (Jordan)
4) Procurement: FinTrust to share expected timelines for contract review so we can align dedicated capacity windows. (Jordan/FinTrust procurement)

A few details that came up that I'll include for the tech call:
- RBAC: role hierarchy (org admin, project admin, developer, auditor, support_readonly) with project-level scoping.
- Break-glass: time-limited elevation with approval workflow, mandatory justification & 2FA for elevated sessions, automatic audit log entry.
- Support access: ephemeral support keys tied to a ticket and auto-revoked; full session recording for elevated sessions available upon request.
- Audit logs: default 90-day retention in the console; longer retention options available as an add-on (365+ days). Logs can be exported to your Splunk/Cloud Storage.

If Wed 10am PT works, I’ll send a calendar invite and attach the documents. Otherwise propose an alternate time.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com

Thanks Marissa — helpful recap. A couple of clarifying questions before the deep-dive so we can prepare our security team: 

- Can you provide a short sample IAM policy or role definitions that show least-privilege mapping for our main personas (SRE, App Dev, Security/Audit, Support)?
- For break-glass, what is the approval model? Is approval required from a FinTrust admin or can it be an internal Redwood escalation with FinTrust notification? We need to ensure no unilateral access without documented approval.
- Audit/logging: you mentioned 90 days by default. Does the audit log capture break-glass justification and originating requester IP/session? We need immutable evidence for investigations.
- Support access: is there a way to gate support engineers by IP or long-lived blocks in addition to ephemeral keys?

If you can attach the SOC2 summary and any RBAC diagrams, that would help our security reviewers ahead of the tech call. Wed 10am PT should be fine — will confirm the attendee list after syncing with Security.

Jordan — thanks, attaching the docs you asked for and answering your questions inline below.

Attachment: redwood-access-controls-overview.pdf (PDF, 3 pages) — includes RBAC role matrix and example IAM policies.
Attachment: redwood-support-access-playbook.pdf (PDF, 5 pages) — describes JIT support flow, ticket gating, and revocation.
Attachment: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (PDF, 2 pages) — SOC 2 Type II scope & link to full report once NDA is in place.

Answers to your questions:
- Sample IAM/roles: included in the access-controls overview. High-level mapping:
  * org_admin — full org-level config and billing
  * project_admin — manage models, deployments, access within project
  * developer — deploy/rollback models, read/write model artifacts
  * auditor — readonly access to logs/metrics/audits
  * support_readonly — view-only access to sessions + ability to open ephemeral debug mode (requires explicit JIT approval)

- Break-glass approval model: by default, break-glass requests trigger a webhook/approval workflow. Options:
  1) FinTrust-controlled approval (preferred for highest assurance): request goes to FinTrust on-call/admin and must approve via SSO or email with justification before elevation.
  2) Redwood-assisted flow: FinTrust can designate a delegated approver list; approvals are recorded and include approver identity and justification.
  In both cases, the event is written to the immutable audit log with the justification and session metadata.

- Audit/logging: yes — break-glass events include user id, requester IP, session id, justification, start/end times, and action transcript where applicable. Logs are tamper-evident and exportable to your SIEM.

- Support access gating: we support IP allowlists at the org level plus ephemeral keys for support engineers. For extra control, you can require that elevated sessions only be initiated from specific IPs or from within your VPC via private peering.

Next steps I propose:
1) I’ll send a calendar invite for Wed 2027-03-17 10:00 AM PT with the deep-dive agenda (RBAC demo, break-glass walkthrough, audit log review).
2) Please share the attendee list (security + SRE + procurement) and any pre-demo questions you want covered.
3) If you need the full SOC 2 report now we can arrange an NDA and DocuSign — let me know.
